a.summary: This is where TransactionRecord's `sign(Signer)` went in the v1_tx refactor, and the hoisted body is the PRE-0d68f02 version: when `numSigners() <= 1` it takes the `else` branch and blindly signs slot 0 via `recordNumSignatures(1); Transaction.sign(signer, data, messageOffset(), messageLength(), signatureOffset(0));` WITHOUT checking that the passed signer is the transaction's required signer. Main commit 0d68f02 deleted exactly that branch. Resolving the TransactionRecord hunk take-theirs therefore silently reverts the fix: a single-signer transaction can again be signed by an arbitrary key and will serialize as validly signed. It also reverts `data[0] = 1` back in place of `data[0] = (byte) numSigners`. Main's test `TransactionSigningTests.singleSignerMustMatchTheRequiredPublicKey` (asserts the wrong signer throws AND that `tx.serialized()` is byte-identical afterwards) fails against this body.

b.summary: VERIFIED (find-string confirmed to occur exactly once in the file). This is where TransactionRecord's `sign(Signer)` went in the v1_tx refactor, and the hoisted body is the PRE-0d68f02 version: when `numSigners() <= 1` it takes the `else` branch and blindly signs slot 0 via `recordNumSignatures(1); Transaction.sign(signer, data, messageOffset(), messageLength(), signatureOffset(0));` WITHOUT checking that the passed signer is the transaction's required signer, and it writes the count 1 rather than the required-signer count. Main commit 0d68f02 deleted exactly that branch. Resolving the TransactionRecord hunk take-theirs therefore silently reverts the fix: a single-signer transaction can again be signed by an arbitrary key and serializes as validly signed. Main's `TransactionSigningTests.singleSignerMustMatchTheRequiredPublicKey` builds a one-signer tx whose non-signer program account is the wrong key, asserts `tx.sign(wrong)` throws IllegalArgumentException containing the key, and asserts `tx.serialized()` is byte-identical afterwards — it fails against this body. Applying the fix in BaseTransaction (rather than re-adding it to TransactionRecord, which cannot override a `final` method) also extends the check to V1Transaction; I verified that is safe and correct: TxBuilderImpl writes `out[1] = (byte) numRequiredSignatures` at build time and lays the sorted, signers-first account list out at V1_ACCOUNTS_OFFSET == accountsOffset(), so `signerIndex` resolves v1 signers exactly as the pre-existing `numSigners() > 1` branch already assumed, and the v1 tests that call `v1Tx.sign(feePayer)`/`sign(signerA)`/`sign(signerB)` (TransactionSerializationTests ~1816, ~1980) all pass keys that are real accounts at their signer index.

instructions.question: How does the defect described by `b` relate to the defect described by `a`?
instructions.focus: Compare the defects, not the wording. Two findings about the same code can still be different defects.

criteria: Different defects: fixing the defect `a` describes would leave the defect `b` describes unfixed, even when both sit in the same code.
The same underlying defect, but `b` narrows it, re-scopes which instances or inputs it covers, or reports it at a different place. Not a different defect in adjacent code.
The same defect restated in different words: fixing one fixes the other.
